content.value_statement: Tamagui projects often fail through small compiler, token, and platform mistakes. This skill gives focused patterns for reliable cross-platform UI work.
actual_capabilities: Guides Tamagui config v4 setup and compiler settings.
Explains compiler-friendly variants, styled components, and prop ordering.
Provides patterns for dialogs, sheets, popovers, tooltips, selects, and forms.
Documents animation drivers, enter and exit styles, and performance settings.
Covers design tokens, themes, typography, spacing, and cross-platform layout.
limitations: It does not run project tests or inspect installed package versions.
Examples may need adjustment for an existing design system.
Some guidance depends on Tamagui v1 behavior and future releases may differ.
Remote documentation fetching is optional and requires network access if used.

use_cases.title: Ship Cross-Platform Screens
use_cases.description: Apply dialog, sheet, overlay, form, and animation patterns that work across web and native targets.

use_cases.title: Standardize UI Foundations
use_cases.description: Define typography, token, theme, and spacing patterns that keep Tamagui components consistent.

use_cases.title: Review Tamagui Code Changes
use_cases.description: Check components for compiler blockers, inline style misuse, token mistakes, and platform-specific gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Tamagui Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Tamagui configuration and identify missing config v4 settings, import issues, and compiler setup risks.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Inline Styles
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this Tamagui component toward styled variants and explain which changes help the compiler optimize it.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Cross-Platform Overlay
prompt_templates.scenario: Dialog, sheet, popover, or select implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Tamagui overlay pattern for web and touch devices, including Adapt behavior and accessibility requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Tamagui Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Tamagui feature for token design, animation performance, form validation, overlay behavior, and compiler compatibility.

output_examples.input: Improve a Tamagui component that uses conditional inline styles.
output: Recommends moving repeatable visual states into variants.
Explains which dynamic values block compiler flattening.
Lists prop-order checks that preserve caller overrides.

output_examples.input: Plan a confirmation dialog that also works on mobile.
output: Provides a dialog and sheet structure using Adapt.
Calls out required title, description, and trigger behavior.
Suggests animation placement on content rather than portal elements.

output_examples.input: Create a design system direction for a Tamagui app.
output: Defines typography, color, and spacing decisions before component work.
Highlights token naming and theme state considerations.
Flags default styling choices that could make the interface feel generic.

best_practices: Read the specific reference file before editing the related UI pattern.
Prefer styled variants for repeatable visual states and compiler-friendly components.
Verify accessibility, Adapt behavior, and platform behavior for forms and overlays.
anti_patterns: Mixing React Native StyleSheet values with Tamagui token props.
Using dynamic inline values where compiler optimization is expected.
Skipping Adapt or PortalProvider when building overlays for touch devices.

faq.question: Which Tamagui version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It focuses on Tamagui v1 patterns, including config v4 and current compiler guidance.

faq.question: Can it generate complete components?
faq.answer: Yes, it can guide component structure, but project-specific styling and testing remain your responsibility.

faq.question: Does it replace the official Tamagui docs?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes practical patterns and can point you toward official documentation when current details matter.

faq.question: Is it useful for React Native projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes native-specific notes for animation drivers, Adapt, sheets, and token resolution.

faq.question: Does it cover form validation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for Tamagui forms, react-hook-form, zod validation, labels, and field state.

faq.question: Will it automatically fetch remote documentation?
faq.answer: No. The skill includes optional curl examples, and remote fetches should require explicit user approval.
